F7: the M0 audit's framing of the defect as a pure race was half the story. The race needs concurrency; the reset->downgrade needs only a single-threaded project switch. The second is the more likely production bite.

F8 (unfixed, reported not silently patched): before this change reset_synapse_memory() propagated a raising save() to its callers (session/tracker.py:115 and ui/panel.py:321 both call it with no try). It now swallows a failing release and logs at ERROR instead. That is a deliberate loudness trade -- an unreleasable handle must not wedge project reload forever -- but it IS a behaviour change on the failure path, and it is named here rather than buried.

F9 (adversarial self-check, prompted by the sibling quartermaster-bisect receipt which roots the test_backfill red in MonetaBackedStore's _jsonl_net dual-write duplicate-append): reset_synapse_memory() now calls MonetaBackedStore.close(), which calls self._jsonl_net.flush() (moneta_store.py:942-946) -- a call the old save()-only reset never made. Checked whether that can duplicate rows. It cannot: MemoryStore.flush -> _flush_writes (store.py:235-267) drains _write_buffer under _write_lock BEFORE writing and only restores lines on a write exception, so repeated flushes are idempotent; and MonetaBackedStore.close() is itself guarded by a _closed flag (moneta_store.py:938-940), so the atexit hook firing after an explicit reset is a no-op rather than a second URI-lock release. The suite agrees: the branch-source-only run is byte-identical to the same-checkout floor, so test_backfill did not get worse.
